intro: Hobbies, family customs, the vocabulary of cooking together, and a few words about thinking things over.
p.el agua.nota: Feminine, but el agua in the singular, like el alma.
p.la sobremesa: time at the table after a meal
b1.texto:
**Hobbies and customs.** **La afición** is what you do for pleasure; **un aficionado** does it for love, not for money. **La costumbre** is what you do regularly; **la tradición** is a custom handed down in a family or a town. **Tener la costumbre de** + infinitive.

**Cooking together.** **La receta**, **el ingrediente**, **la sartén**, **el arroz**, **el caldo**. **Remover** the rice, **probar** the stock, **añadir** salt. **La sobremesa** is the time you stay at the table after eating.

**Gatherings.** **Una comida familiar**, **una fiesta del barrio**, **un concurso de cocina**, **una merienda**, **una excursión**. **Quedar con** los amigos.

**Opinions.** **Creo que** …, **me parece que** …, **estoy convencido de que** … **Dudo que** + subjunctive. **Soñar con** (to dream of).

**Thinking.** **La razón** and **el recuerdo**. **El pensamiento**, **la idea**, **el conocimiento**. **Razonar**, **reflexionar sobre**, **plantearse** una pregunta.

**Probar** has two meanings: to taste and to try.
b2.f0: In many homes in Spain, paella is eaten on Sundays, and fewer and fewer families make it from scratch.
b2.f1: However, during the neighbourhood fiestas the parks fill with improvised kitchens.
b2.f2: Dozens of people stir for hours enormous pans that weigh several kilos, many of them without having cooked all year.
b2.f3: Some do it out of liking, others because of a challenge with friends, and quite a few because their father and grandfather did it.
b2.f4: There are very confident cooks who get emotional when they hear the applause of their neighbourhood.
b2.f5: Whoever wants to understand it should not ask about the recipe but about the company.
b2.f6: For many, paella is not so much a meal as a way of spending the day together.
b4.pregunta: According to the text, why do many people cook at the neighbourhood fiestas?
b4.o0.refuerzo: Porque lo hicieron su padre y su abuelo.
b4.o2.refuerzo: The text does not say that.
b5.pregunta: According to the text, what is paella for many people?
b5.o0.refuerzo: La manera de pasar el día juntos.
b5.o2.refuerzo: The text does not call it a competition.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Un aficionado is an enthusiast: afición means liking, hobby.
b6.o1.refuerzo: A professional would be un profesional.
b7.pregunta: Complete: the water is very hot.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Feminine nouns beginning with stressed a take el in the singular.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Before stressed a, the singular article is el.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Lo is neuter and never goes with a noun.
b8.o0.refuerzo: Probar: to taste, and also to try.
b9.o0: The paella turned out right first time.
b9.o0.explicacion: Salir a la primera means to work out at the first attempt.
b9.o1: The paella came out of the pan first.
b9.o1.explicacion: Salir bien means to turn out well; a la primera is first attempt.
b9.o2: The paella was the first dish served.
b9.o2.explicacion: A la primera means at the first attempt, not first in order.
b10.traduccion: Fewer and fewer families eat together on Sundays.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write an essay on the place of family traditions in a society where fewer and fewer people have time to cook.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Explain aloud a local food tradition of your country to someone who knows nothing about it.
